steps.title: Start at the Dashboard
steps.narration: Every session starts here on the Dashboard — let's head into Research to see what's new this time.
steps.point_out: The familiar left sidebar, with Research as the seventh item.

steps.title: Open the Research hub
steps.narration: Research now has a second card under its governance section — alongside the registry sits a brand-new graveyard of every idea that didn't pan out.
steps.point_out: Below the ten labs and the registry card, a new "Negative-results graveyard" card with an archive icon.

steps.title: Open the negative-results graveyard
steps.narration: This new page lists every idea the system has ever tested and rejected, so nobody wastes time re-deriving a dead idea from scratch.
steps.point_out: Fourteen rows, each with plain-language selectors and a red FAIL badge — and on the ma_stack row, a small "permanent" tag marking it closed for good.

steps.title: See the rule for revisiting a dead idea
steps.narration: Every rejected idea links straight to the one rule that governs whether — and how — it could ever be retested.
steps.point_out: The "Revisit protocol" panel: a closed idea needs a materially new precondition, like two more years of data, before anyone can even propose testing it again.

steps.title: Confirm the original hub is untouched
steps.narration: Heading back to Research shows the original ten labs and the registry exactly where they've always been — the graveyard just joins them, nothing was displaced.
steps.point_out: The same ten lab cards in the same order, starting with "Factor Lab," with both governance cards now sitting together beneath them.

steps.title: Check that nothing else changed
steps.narration: A quick look at the existing Evidence page confirms this new addition didn't disturb anything else in the product.
steps.point_out: All seven tracked claims still show their honest red FAIL badge, exactly as before.

steps.title: Jump straight to the graveyard any time
steps.narration: The new graveyard page also works as a direct link on its own — no need to click through Research every time to find it.
steps.point_out: The same fourteen rows load right away on a fresh visit, each dated 2026-07-03.
